- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecast is rising steadily, reduce forecast slope if true outcome shows early peak then sharp drop (e.g., 2023-12-20, 2024-05-13).  
- If recent sentiment is bearish (≤0.00) and model forecast is flat or rising, adjust downward by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence in “mean reversion” bias.  
- Overshoot after spikes (e.g., 2023-12-20, 2024-05-17) — cap forecast rise after 3–5 consecutive days of high sentiment or high event count.  
- When supply_net is negative and bullish events dominate, model tends to overestimate peak; apply downward bias of 3–8% for 3–7 day horizon.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 2024-05-13–17), model should not overfit to recent trend — use 3-day moving average of sentiment to smooth forecast.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome deviates >5% from 14-day moving average of history, adjust forecast to align with recent volatility (e.g., 2024-05-14, 2024-05-17).  
- When official events are frequent (≥15/30d) and supply_net is negative, forecast should be conservative — reduce slope by 10–20% if sentiment is mixed or bearish.
